provisions.what: Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, the legislature may provide by law for review of determinations of the commission on judicial conduct with respect to justices of town and village courts by an appellate division of the supreme court. In such event, all references in this section to the court of appeals and the chief judge thereof shall be deemed references to an appellate division and the presiding justice thereof, respectively

If a court on the judiciary shall have been convened before the effective date of this section and the proceeding shall not be concluded by that date, the court on the judiciary shall have continuing jurisdiction beyond the effective date of this section to conclude the proceeding
conditions: If a court on the judiciary shall have been convened before the effective date of this section and the proceeding shall not be concluded by that date

provisions.what: All matters pending before the former commission on judicial conduct on the effective date of this section shall be disposed of in such manner as shall be provided by law

review.plain: Judges of the court of appeals and supreme court justices may be removed by a two-thirds vote of both houses; judges of other listed courts by a two-thirds senate vote on the governor's recommendation. Removal requires cause entered on the journals, a statement of the cause, and an opportunity to be heard.
rights: shall have had an opportunity to be heard
powers: may be removed by concurrent resolution of both houses of the legislature
may be removed by the senate, on the recommendation of the governor
limits: No judge or justice shall be removed by virtue of this section except for cause

provisions.what: Judges of the court of appeals and justices of the supreme court may be removed by concurrent resolution of both houses of the legislature, if two-thirds of all the members elected to each house concur therein
conditions: if two-thirds of all the members elected to each house concur therein

provisions.what: Judges of the court of claims, the county court, the surrogate's court, the family court, the courts for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article, the district court and such other courts as the legislature may determine may be removed by the senate, on the recommendation of the governor, if two-thirds of all the members elected to the senate concur therein
conditions: on the recommendation of the governor
if two-thirds of all the members elected to the senate concur therein

provisions.what: No judge or justice shall be removed by virtue of this section except for cause, which shall be entered on the journals, nor unless he or she shall have been served with a statement of the cause alleged, and shall have had an opportunity to be heard
requires: cause, which shall be entered on the journals
served with a statement of the cause alleged
an opportunity to be heard
forbids: Removal by virtue of this section except for cause

provisions.what: On the question of removal, the yeas and nays shall be entered on the journal

review.plain: The assembly may impeach by a majority of all members elected. The senate president, senators and court of appeals judges try impeachments; conviction needs two-thirds of members present. Judgment extends only to removal and disqualification, but the party impeached remains liable to indictment and punishment.
powers: The assembly shall have the power of impeachment
limits: neither the lieutenant-governor nor the temporary president of the senate shall act as a member of the court
No judicial officer shall exercise his or her office
no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of the members present
Judgment in cases of impeachment shall not extend further than to removal from office

provisions.what: The assembly shall have the power of impeachment by a vote of a majority of all the members elected thereto
requires: a vote of a majority of all the members elected thereto

provisions.what: The court for the trial of impeachments shall be composed of the president of the senate, the senators, or the major part of them, and the judges of the court of appeals, or the major part of them
On the trial of an impeachment against the governor or lieutenant-governor, neither the lieutenant-governor nor the temporary president of the senate shall act as a member of the court
provisions.binds: The lieutenant-governor and the temporary president of the senate
conditions: On the trial of an impeachment against the governor or lieutenant-governor

provisions.what: No judicial officer shall exercise his or her office after articles of impeachment against him or her shall have been preferred to the senate, until he or she shall have been acquitted
Before the trial of an impeachment, the members of the court shall take an oath or affirmation truly and impartially to try the impeachment according to the evidence
no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of the members present
requires: the concurrence of two-thirds of the members present

provisions.what: Judgment in cases of impeachment shall not extend further than to removal from office, or removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any public office of honor, trust, or profit under this state
the party impeached shall be liable to indictment and punishment according to law

review.plain: Compensation of the listed judges is set by law and may not be diminished during their term. These judges retire at the end of the year they turn seventy, but former court of appeals judges and supreme court justices may, if certified, serve as supreme court justices until seventy-six.
rights: shall receive without interruption or diminution
powers: may thereafter perform the duties of a justice of the supreme court, with power to hear and determine actions and proceedings
shall be eligible for designation by the governor as a temporary or additional justice of the appellate division
limits: shall not be diminished during the term of office for which he or she was elected or appointed
shall serve no longer than until the last day of December in the year in which he or she reaches the age of seventy-six

provisions.what: The compensation of a judge of the court of appeals, a justice of the supreme court, a judge of the court of claims, a judge of the county court, a judge of the surrogate's court, a judge of the family court, a judge of a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article, a judge of the district court or of a retired judge or justice shall be established by law and shall not be diminished during the term of office for which he or she was elected or appointed
requires: shall be established by law
forbids: Diminishing the compensation during the term of office for which he or she was elected or appointed

provisions.what: Any judge or justice of a court abolished by section thirty-five of this article, who pursuant to that section becomes a judge or justice of a court established or continued by this article, shall receive without interruption or diminution for the remainder of the term for which he or she was elected or appointed to the abolished court the compensation he or she had been receiving upon the effective date of this article together with any additional compensation that may be prescribed by law
provisions.holder: Any judge or justice of a court abolished by section thirty-five of this article who becomes a judge or justice of a court established or continued by this article

provisions.what: Each judge of the court of appeals, justice of the supreme court, judge of the court of claims, judge of the county court, judge of the surrogate's court, judge of the family court, judge of a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article and judge of the district court shall retire on the last day of December in the year in which he or she reaches the age of seventy

Each such former judge of the court of appeals and justice of the supreme court may thereafter perform the duties of a justice of the supreme court, with power to hear and determine actions and proceedings
provisions.holder: Each such former judge of the court of appeals and justice of the supreme court
conditions: provided, however, that it shall be certificated in the manner provided by law that the services of such judge or justice are necessary to expedite the business of the court and that he or she is mentally and physically able and competent to perform the full duties of such office

provisions.what: Any such certification shall be valid for a term of two years and may be extended as provided by law for additional terms of two years
A retired judge or justice shall serve no longer than until the last day of December in the year in which he or she reaches the age of seventy-six
A retired judge or justice shall be subject to assignment by the appellate division of the supreme court of the judicial department of his or her residence

Any retired justice of the supreme court who had been designated to and served as a justice of any appellate division immediately preceding his or her reaching the age of seventy shall be eligible for designation by the governor as a temporary or additional justice of the appellate division
conditions: who had been designated to and served as a justice of any appellate division immediately preceding his or her reaching the age of seventy

provisions.what: A retired judge or justice shall not be counted in determining the number of justices in a judicial district for purposes of subdivision d of section six of this article

The provisions of this section shall also be applicable to any judge or justice who has not reached the age of seventy-six and to whom it would otherwise have been applicable but for the fact that he or she reached the age of seventy and retired before the effective date of this article

review.plain: Judges and justices of the listed courts may perform their duties or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the courts named. The chief administrator of the courts makes the assignments, and an assigned judge has the powers of the court to which assigned.
powers: A justice of the supreme court may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county
may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in any judicial district or to the court of claims
shall be made by the chief administrator of the courts
may provide for temporary assignments within the county of residence or any adjoining county
also may be temporarily assigned by the chief administrator of the courts
shall have the powers, duties and jurisdiction of a judge or justice of the court to which assigned

provisions.what: A justice of the supreme court may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in any judicial district or to the court of claims
provisions.holder: A justice of the supreme court

provisions.what: A justice of the supreme court in the city of New York may be temporarily assigned to the family court in the city of New York or to the surrogate's court in any county within the city of New York when required to dispose of the business of such court
provisions.holder: A justice of the supreme court in the city of New York
conditions: when required to dispose of the business of such court

provisions.what: A judge of the court of claims may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in any judicial district
provisions.holder: A judge of the court of claims

provisions.what: A judge of the county court may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in the judicial department of his or her residence or to the county court or the family court in any county or to the surrogate's court in any county outside the city of New York or to a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article
provisions.holder: A judge of the county court

provisions.what: A judge of the surrogate's court in any county within the city of New York may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in the judicial department of his or her residence
provisions.holder: A judge of the surrogate's court in any county within the city of New York

provisions.what: A judge of the surrogate's court in any county outside the city of New York may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in the judicial department of his or her residence or to the county court or the family court in any county or to a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article
provisions.holder: A judge of the surrogate's court in any county outside the city of New York

provisions.what: A judge of the family court may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in the judicial department of his or her residence or to the county court or the family court in any county or to the surrogate's court in any county outside of the city of New York or to a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article
provisions.holder: A judge of the family court

provisions.what: A judge of a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in the judicial department of his or her residence or to the county court or the family court in any county or to the other court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article
provisions.holder: A judge of a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article

provisions.what: A judge of the district court in any county may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the county court in the judicial department of his or her residence or to a court for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article or to the district court in any county
provisions.holder: A judge of the district court in any county

provisions.what: Temporary assignments of all the foregoing judges or justices listed in this section, and of judges of the city courts pursuant to paragraph two of subdivision j of this section, shall be made by the chief administrator of the courts in accordance with standards and administrative policies established pursuant to section twenty-eight of this article
provisions.holder: The chief administrator of the courts
conditions: in accordance with standards and administrative policies established pursuant to section twenty-eight of this article

provisions.what: The legislature may provide for temporary assignments within the county of residence or any adjoining county, of judges of town, village or city courts outside the city of New York

In addition to any temporary assignments to which a judge of a city court may be subject pursuant to paragraph one of this subdivision, such judge also may be temporarily assigned by the chief administrator of the courts to the county court, the family court or the district court within his or her county of residence or any adjoining county provided he or she is not permitted to practice law
provisions.holder: The chief administrator of the courts
conditions: provided he or she is not permitted to practice law

provisions.what: While temporarily assigned pursuant to the provisions of this section, any judge or justice shall have the powers, duties and jurisdiction of a judge or justice of the court to which assigned

After the expiration of any temporary assignment, as provided in this section, the judge or justice assigned shall have all the powers, duties and jurisdiction of a judge or justice of the court to which he or she was assigned with respect to matters pending before him or her during the term of such temporary assignment

review.plain: The governor may appoint extraordinary terms of the supreme court when in the governor's opinion the public interest requires, designating the time, place and justice. The governor may end the justice's assignment and name another justice.
powers: may, when in his or her opinion the public interest requires, appoint extraordinary terms of the supreme court
may terminate the assignment of the justice

provisions.what: The governor may, when in his or her opinion the public interest requires, appoint extraordinary terms of the supreme court
conditions: when in his or her opinion the public interest requires

provisions.what: The governor shall designate the time and place of holding the term and the justice who shall hold the term
The governor may terminate the assignment of the justice and may name another justice in his or her place to hold the term

review.plain: The chief judge of the court of appeals is the chief judge of the state and heads the unified court system, with an administrative board of the courts. The chief judge appoints a chief administrator, who supervises the court system, and sets standards and policies approved by the court of appeals.
powers: appoint a chief administrator of the courts who shall serve at the pleasure of the chief judge
shall supervise the administration and operation of the unified court system
shall establish standards and administrative policies for general application throughout the state

provisions.what: The chief judge of the court of appeals shall be the chief judge of the state of New York and shall be the chief judicial officer of the unified court system

There shall be an administrative board of the courts which shall consist of the chief judge of the court of appeals as chairperson and the presiding justice of the appellate division of the supreme court of each judicial department
The chief judge shall, with the advice and consent of the administrative board of the courts, appoint a chief administrator of the courts who shall serve at the pleasure of the chief judge
requires: the advice and consent of the administrative board of the courts

provisions.what: The chief administrator, on behalf of the chief judge, shall supervise the administration and operation of the unified court system

In the exercise of such responsibility, the chief administrator of the courts shall have such powers and duties as may be delegated to him or her by the chief judge and such additional powers and duties as may be provided by law
provisions.holder: The chief administrator of the courts

provisions.what: The chief judge, after consultation with the administrative board, shall establish standards and administrative policies for general application throughout the state, which shall be submitted by the chief judge to the court of appeals, together with the recommendations, if any, of the administrative board
requires: after consultation with the administrative board

provisions.what: Such standards and administrative policies shall be promulgated after approval by the court of appeals
requires: approval by the court of appeals

review.plain: The legislature must provide for allocating the cost of running the listed courts among the state, counties, New York City and other subdivisions, and for submitting court budget estimates. The legislature and governor, or the local governing bodies, make the final determination for the expenses each bears.
powers: shall be made by the legislature and the governor
shall be made by the appropriate governing bodies

provisions.what: The legislature shall provide for the allocation of the cost of operating and maintaining the court of appeals, the appellate division of the supreme court in each judicial department, the supreme court, the court of claims, the county court, the surrogate's court, the family court, the courts for the city of New York established pursuant to section fifteen of this article and the district court, among the state, the counties, the city of New York and other political subdivisions

The legislature shall provide for the submission of the itemized estimates of the annual financial needs of the courts referred to in subdivision a of this section to the chief administrator of the courts to be forwarded to the appropriating bodies with recommendations and comment

Insofar as the expense of the courts is borne by the state or paid by the state in the first instance, the final determination of the itemized estimates of the annual financial needs of the courts shall be made by the legislature and the governor in accordance with articles four and seven of this constitution
conditions: Insofar as the expense of the courts is borne by the state or paid by the state in the first instance
in accordance with articles four and seven of this constitution

provisions.what: Insofar as the expense of the courts is not paid by the state in the first instance and is borne by counties, the city of New York or other political subdivisions, the final determination of the itemized estimates of the annual financial needs of the courts shall be made by the appropriate governing bodies of such counties, the city of New York or other political subdivisions
provisions.holder: The appropriate governing bodies of such counties, the city of New York or other political subdivisions
conditions: Insofar as the expense of the courts is not paid by the state in the first instance and is borne by counties, the city of New York or other political subdivisions

review.plain: The legislature keeps its power to alter and regulate court jurisdiction and proceedings, and may delegate its power over practice and procedure to a court or the chief administrator of the courts. Individual courts may still adopt regulations consistent with general practice and procedure.
powers: shall have the same power to alter and regulate the jurisdiction and proceedings in law and in equity
delegate, in whole or in part, to a court

provisions.what: The legislature shall have the same power to alter and regulate the jurisdiction and proceedings in law and in equity that it has heretofore exercised

The legislature may, on such terms as it shall provide and subject to subsequent modification, delegate, in whole or in part, to a court, including the appellate division of the supreme court, or to the chief administrator of the courts, any power possessed by the legislature to regulate practice and procedure in the courts
conditions: on such terms as it shall provide and subject to subsequent modification

provisions.what: The chief administrator of the courts shall exercise any such power delegated to him or her with the advice and consent of the administrative board of the courts
provisions.binds: The chief administrator of the courts
requires: the advice and consent of the administrative board of the courts

provisions.what: Nothing herein contained shall prevent the adoption of regulations by individual courts consistent with the general practice and procedure as provided by statute or general rules
conditions: consistent with the general practice and procedure as provided by statute or general rules

review.plain: Article VI does not apply to the peacemakers courts or other Indian courts, which continue to exist and operate as provided by law.
limits: This article does not apply to the peacemakers courts or other Indian courts

provisions.what: This article does not apply to the peacemakers courts or other Indian courts, the existence and operation of which shall continue as may be provided by law

review.plain: When a court commits, remands or places a child in its jurisdiction with an institution, agency or person, the child must be placed, when practicable, with an institution or agency governed by persons, or a person, of the same religious persuasion as the child.
rights: of the same religious persuasion as the child

provisions.what: When any court having jurisdiction over a child shall commit it or remand it to an institution or agency or place it in the custody of any person by parole, placing out, adoption or guardianship, the child shall be committed or remanded or placed, when practicable, in an institution or agency governed by persons, or in the custody of a person, of the same religious persuasion as the child
provisions.binds: Any court having jurisdiction over a child
conditions: when practicable

review.plain: Existing laws not inconsistent with this article stay in force until changed under it. The legislature must enact laws to carry out the article and may enact other laws, not inconsistent with it, to implement, supplement or clarify its provisions.
powers: may, for the purpose of implementing, supplementing or clarifying any of its provisions, enact any laws

provisions.what: Existing provisions of law not inconsistent with this article shall continue in force until repealed, amended, modified or superseded in accordance with the provisions of this article
The legislature shall enact appropriate laws to carry into effect the purposes and provisions of this article

The legislature may, for the purpose of implementing, supplementing or clarifying any of its provisions, enact any laws, not inconsistent with the provisions of this article, necessary or desirable in promoting the objectives of this article
conditions: not inconsistent with the provisions of this article
